title: Knotted, or just looped?
hook: A hair tie caught on a cord looks like a knot. How do you get it off?

knows: Everyday objects have sizes, positions and amounts
doesNotKnow: that a crossing is not a knot if the loop can slide off an open end, so sliding it off frees the cord

misconception: A loop that crosses itself is a knot that has to be picked apart or cut.
objective: A hair tie round a cord is a closed loop, not a knot, so there is nothing to pick apart. While the cord's end is free, the loop slides along the cord and off the end, and the cord lies straight again.

claims.text: A hair tie round a cord is a closed loop, not a knot, so there is nothing to pick apart. While the cord's end is free, the loop slides along the cord and off the end, and the cord lies straight again.
claims.source: W-383 (2026-10-14, demo-builder): retyped from source (Raymer & Smith 2007, which could not be opened from this host) to derivation, as FC LH-1 and FC LH-2 asked. Argument: the drawn curl is a one-crossing diagram of an open arc (a Reidemeister I kink). A one-crossing diagram is never a knot, so the crossing alone does not prove a knot. The cord has a free end, so the loop can be slid along the cord and off that end, which removes the crossing without cutting; on the stage the free end (15 to 35 cm on the slider) always exceeds the 10 cm loop travel (src/lib/lifehacks/home-models.ts evaluateHome, homeCordScene). Earlier history: FC LH-2 held it unverified only because its sole source was unopenable. | FC pass 35 (fact-checker, 2026-10-14): VERIFIED. Read the cord scene in HomeLesson.tsx and homeCordScene first. Derivation: an arc with free ends is unknotted (any tangle in an open string can be undone by moving an end), and the drawn curl is a one-crossing kink (Reidemeister I), so one crossing never proves a knot. Own run of the transpiled home-models.ts: crossings = 1 before and 0 after 'Slide loop off'. The free end minus the start is 3p px for p = 15 to 35 cm, always more than the 10 cm loop travel (30 px). The reveal shows spec.idea, the claim text. No source is relied on. Reset to unverified 2026-10-16 by demo-builder (r11 fix plan wave W3: new prediction line, stage and reveal; engine 2). Re-verify against the rebuilt stage. | FC pass 54 (fact-checker, 2026-10-16): VERIFIED. Derivation re-checked: a closed elastic loop around an open arc with a free end can be slid along and off that end (an arc is unknotted and unlinked from anything once an end is free), so nothing needs picking apart or cutting. Rendered reveal matches the text word for word. No source relied on. recall.question: A drawn cord crosses over itself, and the loop's free end is within reach. What does the lesson say about whether this is a knot?
options: Yes: one crossing is enough to prove a knot
Not if the loop slides off the free end
Yes: only cutting can remove the crossing
recall.why: A crossing in a drawing does not prove a knot. An open loop can slide off an accessible end, and the crossing disappears without cutting.
